messages.author: 7e496b53938e5e54
messages.subject: readModels tech1 error
parts:
Hi,
I am using readModels in order to obtain the parameter numbers from tech1.
When I use the following code to read in the models, and when I view or try to manipulate tech1 results, I get the wrong parameter numbers when I compare to the output.

I read in the file like this:

modelResults <- readModels("M:/CONTEXT/Code/Scoring/alc_final.out")

When I print modelResults and compare with output, they do not match.

First line from tech1 tau output (Mplus):

           TAU
              C_AUSE2$      C_AUSE2$      C_AUSE2$      C_AUSE3$      C_AUSE3$
              ________      ________      ________      ________      ________
 1                 23            24            25            26            27


   versus first line from tech1 from readModels:
$parameterSpecification
$X
$tau
  C_AUSE2$ C_AUSE2$ C_AUSE2$ C_AUSE3$ C_AUSE3$ C_AUSE3$ C_AUSE3$ C_AUSE4$
1       25       NA       NA       29       NA       NA       NA       32


Any advice on this problem would be very much appreciated!
Thank you,
Nisha

messages.author: 644e1c01c3c42210
messages.subject: Re: readModels tech1 error
parts:
Hi Nisha,

This is a tricky one. I looked over your .out file, and the challenge is that Mplus does not output unique column names in the tech1 section. This comes from Mplus setting a hard limit of 8 characters on its column output (whereas your thresholds here are presumably $1 $2 etc.). I have written a workaround for non-unique column names in matrix-like sections and committed it to Github: https://github.com/michaelhallquist/MplusAutomation. You can install the development version using the instructions there. This led to your TECH1 section being imported properly. The workaround works for non-unique column names, but would still break down for non-unique row names. I don't have time to figure that one out at the moment... In such a case, you should shorten your variable names to 6 characters to make space for the $1 $2 etc.

Best,
Michael
